description: Personal AI efficiency dashboard. Weekly and monthly review of prompting efficiency, credit spend, model usage, and code output. Data has a 2-day lag from GitHub API.

options.content:
## My Copilot AI Efficiency Tracker

This dashboard helps you understand how efficiently you are using GitHub Copilot and AI credits over time. It is designed for **weekly and monthly review** — not real-time monitoring.

**Data lag:** All data has a **2-day lag** from GitHub's API. The most recent data visible today reflects activity from 2 days ago. This is a GitHub API limitation and cannot be changed by the exporter.

**Best use pattern**
- **Weekly (Monday morning):** Review last week's efficiency ratios — LOC per prompt, credit per LOC, acceptance rate. Check which models you used most.
- **Monthly:** Review your 30-day trend lines. Are your efficiency ratios improving? Is your acceptance rate rising? Are you spending credits on the right models?

**The three efficiency ratios to focus on**
- **LOC per Prompt** — lines of accepted code per prompt sent. Rising = your prompts are improving.
- **Credit per LOC** — AI credits spent per line of accepted code. Falling = you are getting more code for less spend.
- **Acceptance Rate** — proportion of AI suggestions you accepted. Rising = better model fit or better prompting.

Select your **Enterprise** and **GitHub Username** from the dropdowns above. Set your **Monthly AI Credit Budget** if your team has an allocation.

panels.title: Total Prompts
panels.description: Total Copilot prompts and interactions across all surfaces in the selected window. Source: github_copilot_user_prompt_count.

panels.title: Total LOC Added
panels.description: Total lines of AI-generated code you accepted in the selected window. Primary output productivity signal. Source: github_copilot_user_loc_added_sum.

panels.title: AI Credits Used
panels.description: Total AI credits consumed in the selected window. Credits apply to premium model requests only. 1 AI Credit = $0.01 USD. Source: github_copilot_user_ai_credits_used.

panels.title: Monthly Credit Budget Used
panels.description: AI credits consumed in the last 30 days as a percentage of your entered monthly budget. Green = within budget, amber = approaching limit, red = over 90%. Set the budget using the field above.

panels.title: Acceptance Rate
panels.description: Ratio of code acceptance to code generation activities in the selected window. Higher means more AI suggestions are being accepted. A rising trend over time indicates improving prompt quality. Source: acceptance_count / generation_count.

panels.title: My Efficiency Ratios — The Metrics That Matter

options.content: These three ratios are your AI efficiency score. **LOC per Prompt rising** means each prompt produces more accepted code — your prompting is improving. **Credit per LOC falling** means you are getting more code per dollar spent — better model selection or more efficient prompting. **Acceptance Rate rising** means you are accepting more of what Copilot offers — better model fit or better scoping of requests. All three are calculated from completed daily data with a 2-day lag. Review these weekly on Monday morning for the most complete picture of last week.

panels.title: LOC per Prompt (30d)
panels.description: Lines of accepted AI code per prompt sent over the last 30 days. This is your primary prompting efficiency score. A higher number means each prompt you send produces more usable code. Target: rising trend over time. Source: loc_added_sum / prompt_count.

panels.title: Credit per LOC Added (30d)
panels.description: AI credits spent per line of accepted code over the last 30 days. Lower is better — it means you are getting more code output per credit spent. A rising number means increasing cost per line, which may indicate over-use of premium models for simple tasks. Source: ai_credits_used / loc_added_sum.

panels.title: Acceptance Rate (30d)
panels.description: Percentage of AI code suggestions you accepted over the last 30 days. A rising trend indicates improving prompt quality — you are getting suggestions that are more worth keeping. Target: above 30% is healthy, above 50% is excellent. Source: acceptance_activity_count / generation_activity_count.

panels.title: My Efficiency Trends — Are You Improving Over Time?
LOC per Prompt — Weekly Trend
panels.description: Your prompting efficiency over time. Each data point is the LOC-per-prompt ratio for that day, smoothed over a 7-day rolling window. A rising trend is the goal — it means each prompt you send produces progressively more accepted code. Dips may indicate days spent on exploratory or conversational tasks rather than code generation. Source: 7-day rolling loc_added_sum / prompt_count.

panels.title: Credit per LOC — Monthly Trend
panels.description: Your AI credit cost efficiency over time. Each data point is credits spent per line of accepted code, smoothed over a 30-day rolling window. A falling trend means you are getting progressively more code output per credit spent. Rising values may indicate a shift toward heavier premium models or lower code acceptance. Source: 30-day rolling ai_credits_used / loc_added_sum.

panels.title: Acceptance Rate — Daily Trend
panels.description: Your code acceptance rate each day over the selected window. A rising long-term trend is strong evidence that your prompting technique is improving. Short-term dips are normal and often reflect complex tasks where AI suggestions are less directly applicable. Source: daily acceptance_activity_count / generation_activity_count.

panels.title: Daily LOC Suggested vs Accepted
panels.description: Lines of code Copilot suggested versus lines you actually accepted each day. The gap between the two shows how selective you are. A narrowing gap over time means you are accepting more of what Copilot offers — either because your prompts are better targeted or because the model is fitting your workflow more closely. Source: loc_suggested_to_add_sum and loc_added_sum.

panels.title: My Daily Prompt Count
panels.description: Number of Copilot prompts you submitted each day. Gaps indicate days with no usage. Spikes typically correspond to heavy feature development or debugging sessions. Data has a 2-day lag — today and yesterday will not appear. Source: github_copilot_user_prompt_count.

panels.title: My Daily AI Credits Used
panels.description: AI credits consumed each day. Credits apply only to premium model usage. Days showing zero may indicate standard model usage rather than no activity — standard models do not consume credits. Data has a 2-day lag. Source: github_copilot_user_ai_credits_used.

panels.title: My Prompts by Model
panels.description: Distribution of prompts across models. If premium models (Claude Opus, GPT-4o) dominate for routine tasks, switching to standard models for those tasks would reduce credit consumption without impacting output quality. Source: github_copilot_user_model_feature_prompt_count grouped by model.

panels.title: My Prompts by Feature
panels.description: Distribution of prompts across Copilot features (completions, chat, CLI, code review). Shows which surfaces you rely on most. Source: github_copilot_user_feature_prompt_count grouped by feature.

panels.title: My Top Languages by LOC Added
panels.description: Top 10 programming languages where you accepted the most AI-generated code. Reflects where Copilot delivers the most output value for your specific work. Source: github_copilot_user_language_feature_loc_added_sum grouped by language.

panels.title: My Credit Intelligence — Are You Spending on the Right Things?

options.content: These panels answer the question: **are you spending AI credits on the right tasks with the right models?** If your most expensive model is also your most productive one (highest LOC per prompt), the spend is justified. If an expensive model produces the same LOC per prompt as a cheaper one, switch models for that task type. Review this section monthly when comparing your credit spend to your code output.

panels.title: My Cumulative Credit Spend This Month
panels.description: Running total of AI credits consumed since the start of the selected window. Use this to track spend against your monthly budget allocation and forecast whether you will exceed it before month end. Data has a 2-day lag so the current day's spend is not yet visible. Source: cumulative sum of github_copilot_user_ai_credits_used.

panels.title: My Credit Spend by Model
panels.description: Total AI credits consumed per model over the selected window. Identifies which models are driving your personal credit spend. Compare to your LOC-per-prompt by model to determine whether expensive model usage is justified by proportionally higher code output. Source: github_copilot_user_model_feature_prompt_count used as proxy — note: per-user per-model credit breakdown is not directly available from GitHub API; this uses prompt count as a relative indicator.

panels.title: My Prompts by IDE
panels.description: Breakdown of your Copilot prompts by IDE over the selected window. Shows which development environment you use most with Copilot. Source: github_copilot_user_ide_prompt_count grouped by ide.

panels.title: My LOC Added by IDE
panels.description: Lines of AI-generated code accepted per IDE. Shows where Copilot delivers the most code output in your workflow. Source: github_copilot_user_ide_loc_added_sum grouped by ide.
